sound_plan.note: Recorded sounds for the floating-city film (pipeline/sound.py). Owner request 2026-11-12: add the Pixabay sounds proposed in review/SFX_LIBRARY.md, only where they fit the channel's explanatory style. The owner downloaded the candidates; the agent chose one file per place by measurement (length, onset, noise floor, low/high balance, steadiness), not by listening. The owner listens and decides.

SINK.why: one clean, low 'splosh' (most energy under 250 Hz): the block goes under, no splash from height

PLACE.why: the fifth of seven soft thuds (the strongest, floor 58 dB under it): a storey set down

PLACE_HEAVY.why: a single deep wooden thud, cleaner and lower than PLACE: the deeper hull

PLACE_LIGHT.why: a single light, short 'place': the walkway set across the gap, the lightest of the four

CHAPTER.why: the smoothest of the soft air whooshes (almost nothing above 2.5 kHz): marks the cut, not a sound effect to notice

WATER_A.why: the steadiest 12 s of the recording (its loudest 0.2 s within 8.8 dB of the median)

WATER_B.why: the steadiest 8 s of the recording

cues.why: B05 'sinks': the solid block, flush with the surface, starts down to the seabed
B13: the hinged walkway lands across the gap

chapter_cues.why: chapters 2-8: the whoosh peaks 0.1 s before the cut, in the 1.2 s without speech around it

beds.why: B17: five platforms rise, fall and tilt on the water
B30: the long swell along the breakwater, until the camera is down at the level view
